title: Rav Shmuel bar Idi
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: In Taanit 9a it is told that Rav Huna bar Manoach, Rav Shmuel bar Idi, and Rav Chiya of Vostanya were frequently present before Rava. When he passed away, they came before Rav Papa. Whenever he told them a halakhic tradition and it did not seem reasonable to them, they would hint to one another. This pained him, and the verse was read to him in his dream, "And I destroyed the three shepherds." The next day, as they were taking leave of him, he said to them, "Let the rabbis go in peace" (so it appears in Ein Yaakov, and the intent is that he blessed them that they should live).
And in Pesachim 104a, Rav Shmuel bar Idi sent word: "My brother Chananya says one" (and see the entry Chananya bar Idi).

But what we find in Vayikra Rabbah 14:2, "Rabbi Shmuel bar Idi in the name of Rabbi Acha," Hyman says should be corrected there to "Rabbi Shmuel bar Unya," as in Yalkut, Job, remez 902 (printed: תתקב).

notes.text: Hyman attributes the farewell wording לשלמא to Ein Yaakov. The checked vocalized William Davidson text of Taanit 9b has בשלמא. The narrative begins on 9a and continues on 9b.

The dream and farewell continuation was independently read at Taanit 9b; it follows 9a. Hyman’s Ein Yaakov reading לשלמא remains attributed to him because that exact edition was not independently inspected; the consulted text has בשלמא. His Unya/Yalkut emendation remains his proposed correction.
